subject: Next steps: dedicated reservation priority map & SLO requests (HelixThera)
messages:
From: Sam Cooper <sam.cooper@helixthera.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Linda Park <linda.park@helixthera.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's capacity call

Thanks again for the deep dive this morning — useful session. A few things we want to capture on our side so we stay aligned: 

- Primary pain: latency and cold-start variability during peak inference (even with smaller batch sizes). This is impacting customer-facing SLA promises.
- Isolation requirement: some workloads will carry PHI; we need tenant-level isolation and encryption-in-transit + at-rest controls.
- Throughput profile: steady-state 18–22 TPS for our realtime endpoint, with spikes up to ~80 TPS during daytime bursts.
- Preferred timeline: pilot in Q3, production by late Q4 if commercial terms are agreeable.

Can you confirm what a reserved pool that meets steady-state + burst looks like (rough sizing, SLO targets you recommend), and what the fallback path is if we exceed reserved capacity? Also please include any security onboarding steps we should expect.

Sam
Product & Ops
HelixThera
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cooper <sam.cooper@helixthera.com>
Cc: Linda Park <linda.park@helixthera.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's capacity call

Hi Sam — great talking earlier. Below is a concise post-call recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum. Please reply with any corrections.

Recap of pain & goals
- Latency variability during bursts is the top ops risk; you need predictable p95/p99 under peak traffic.
- Isolation & compliance: tenant isolation for PHI workloads, KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2-related evidence.
- Target throughput: steady 18–22 TPS; design for sustained 80 TPS burst windows of up to 10–15 minutes.
- Timeline: Q3 pilot -> Q4 production (aligned).

Prelim sizing recommendation (reserved + burst)
- Reserved pool: 4x GPU nodes (A100-type equivalent), configured as a private pool (dedicated tenant lanes) to guarantee steady throughput and KV cache locality. This should cover ~20 TPS steady with low p99.
- Burst capacity: configurable burst to an additional 6 nodes (best-effort reserved burst) managed by autoscaling policy with pre-warmed containers for fast ramp. Burst would be billed as overage or via short-term bursting credits in a committed plan.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to a quantized model variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost if capacity constraints are hit; we can also set hard throttles per-route.

SLOs we recommend
- 99.9% availability (platform-level for dedicated pools)
- p95 latency target: <= 120ms for the realtime endpoint under steady-state
- p99: <= 350ms under normal load; we can set an elevated p99 SLA for burst windows with a separate contractual window.

Security & onboarding
- We'll initiate our SOC 2 evidence package and a short questionnaire (Neha will kick off).
- KMS integration: support for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key).

Attachments: I attached a capacity estimate and a draft SLA for your review (see list below).

Proposed next steps (short list)
1) Technical deep-dive (ops + infra) — action: Sean to propose a 60-min session; we need peak traces + sample payloads from you.
2) Security onboarding — action: Neha to send SOC2 questionnaire and list of required evidence.
3) Commercial path — action: Ben to surface a draft SOW and pricing for reserved + burst options; review with your procurement.
4) Timeline check: target pilot sign-off by 2026-08-15 to meet Q3 pilot timeline.

If that looks right I can schedule the two follow-ups (technical and security) and loop in our SRE on the call.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Direct: 415-555-0191

Attachments:
- HelixThera_capacity_estimate_q3.pdf (est sizing & cost)
- Redwood_SLA-draft-v1.docx
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sam Cooper <sam.cooper@helixthera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's capacity call

Adding a couple of technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side so HelixThera's infra team has something concrete ahead of the deep-dive: 

- Cache behavior: dedicated pools get local KV cache affinity which materially reduces cold-start p99s for repeated prefixes — this will help your steady-state p95.
- Pre-warm strategy: we recommend warm pools for known daytime burst windows; we can pre-warm a fraction of burst nodes to reduce spin-up from ~45s to ~6–8s.
- Network isolation: we will enable private VPC connectivity with egress controls for PHI endpoints; KMS-backed disk encryption is supported.
- Observability: we'll instrument per-route token-level latency and a night-ops alert that triggers when p99 crosses 300ms for >5 minutes.

Operational asks for the deep-dive:
- Sample peak-hour traces (timestamps + qps series) and a couple of representative payloads.
- Any hard per-user rate limits you need enforced.

I'll put together a short runbook draft for warm-up + fallback routing that we can review on the tech call.

-sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cooper <sam.cooper@helixthera.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: dedicated reservation priority map & SLO requests (HelixThera)

Sam / Linda — following Rachel's recap and Sean's notes, next steps from commercial & procurement: 

- I'll draft a simple SOW that includes: reserved pool (4 nodes), burst tranche (up to 6 nodes), billing model (commit + burst credits), and the SLO appendix Rachel proposed. Expect the first draft by EOD Friday.
- Procurement ask: please confirm preferred PO process and contact at HelixThera (billing@ or procurement@).
- For timelines: to hit a Q3 pilot we recommend finalizing commercial terms by 2026-07-20 and starting onboarding the following week.

Neha — can you open the SOC2 questionnaire ticket for HelixThera and share the expected evidence timeline?

Sam — quick question: do you want the pilot to be in our hosted dedicated environment (Redwood-managed private pool) or fully private in your VPC? We should decide before we lock the SOW.

Thanks — Ben
